newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai people save more, spend less on food.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai people save more, spend less on food.

text.p: The average income of Shanghai residents has risen sharply over the past 16 years, with people saving more and spending less on food, the Liberation Daily reported on Monday.
The average monthly income in 1996 reached 646.14 yuan, up from 46.65 yuan in 1980, an inflation-adjusted increase of 7.1 percent a year, it said.
Average monthly expenditure has risen to 555.27 yuan in 1996 from 46.07 yuan in 1980, with spending on food falling to 43.3 percent of total expenditure from 55.3 percent in 1980, it said.
The figures show that Shanghai people are putting more money into the bank and spending more on consumer products other than food, it said but gave no more details.
